overall: Washington DC is warming steadily from a morning low near 73°F, with the current running max at 77°F as of 08:52 ET and a positive velocity of +1.8°F/hr suggesting continued heating into the afternoon. Skies are mostly clear (FEW clouds, ~62% cloud fraction), supporting good solar insolation during the critical late-morning and early-afternoon heating window. However, scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop by 3–5 PM ET, which introduces a meaningful risk of cutting off the warming before reaching the NWS-forecast peak of 93°F.
forecast_obs_notes: Models are notably split: HRRR is the most aggressive at 93.3°F (aligning closely with the NWS 93°F text forecast), while ECMWF (89.9°F) and NBM (88.5°F) are considerably cooler, reflecting uncertainty around afternoon convection timing. The META model — the most reliable fused signal — concentrates probability in the 86–89°F range (combined ~56%), notably cooler than both the NWS narrative and the D1_NOW distribution, which is heavily skewed toward 90–91°F (61.4%) driven by HRRR.
max_temp_prediction: The active Kalshi market uses even buckets, with the top even bucket at 90–91°F (61.4% per D1_NOW). However, the META model tempers this view significantly, favoring 86–89°F and assigning only 17% to 90–91°F. Balancing the HRRR-driven D1_NOW bullishness against the META model's caution and the real threat of early convective cloud cover and storms suppressing the afternoon peak, a best estimate of around 90°F feels appropriate — consistent with the top even bucket but near its lower boundary. Confidence is moderate: if storms fire before 3 PM, the high could drop into the 86–89°F range; if storms hold off until 5 PM or later, 91–93°F remains possible.
